NVDA.short: Nvidia reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier (up 20% from the prior quarter). It forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $130.0 billion, plus or minus 3%, with no China Data Center compute revenue assumed.

NVDA.short: On November 11, 2026, Nvidia said CEO Jensen Huang resigned effective immediately. CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO while keeping her CFO role during a search for a permanent CEO, and Harvey Jones was named Chair. Earnings are still set for November 17.

short.AMD: Most of these are opinion pieces, but they cite some real events: AMD reported Q3 revenue of $13.4 billion, up 45%, with data center revenue up 97%, and completed an $8.2 billion acquisition of World Labs. The stock still fell, including 4.4% after new U.S. export restrictions on Southeast Asia, where Singapore was 12.4% of 2025 revenue. Writers disagree on whether AMD's valuation is justified.
short.NVDA: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on November 12 after an affair scandal, including alleged ties to a suspected Chinese spy, and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Despite this, Q3 revenue was $115.8 billion, up 103%, and growth guidance was raised to 75%. The stock has fallen sharply, and the articles are opinion pieces that disagree on whether leadership risk or strong results matter more.
short.META: These articles are mostly opinion pieces, with no single new company event. One factual thread is that Meta borrowed about $25 billion this month, lifting debt to roughly $109 billion while spending heavily on AI (2026 capex of $135-145B). Commentators disagree: some stress strong ad growth and a modest valuation, others warn of shrinking margins and Reality Labs losses.
